key_insight: Representing object interactions in a persistent 3D world-frame (4D: 3D + time) from monocular video enables scene graphs that reason through occlusions and over time, rather than being limited to single 2D frames.
problem_solved: Existing scene-graph methods are frame-centric: they operate in 2D, drop objects when occluded, and cannot model persistent, world-referenced interactions across time. This work provides a dataset and approach to build spatio‑temporal, world‑centric scene graphs from monocular video.
method: ActionGenome4D dataset: upgrade Action Genome videos into 4D scenes via feed‑forward 3D reconstruction and world‑frame oriented bounding boxes and dense relational annotations for all action objects.
World‑centric scene graph generation: infer object locations and relations in a fixed world frame across time (3D + temporal links), enabling object permanence and occlusion handling.
Temporal and 3D-aware relation modeling: aggregate temporal cues and 3D geometry (tracking, poses, world transforms) to predict spatio‑temporal edges and evolving interactions.
impact: Provides practitioners with a benchmark and methods to build persistent, 3D-aware scene graphs from ordinary monocular video — useful for robotics, AR/VR, long-horizon video understanding, and any system needing durable scene reasoning across occlusions and time.

paper_title: Towards Spatio-Temporal World Scene Graph Generation from Monocular Videos
paper_authors: Rohith Peddi, Saurabh, Shravan Shanmugam, Likhitha Pallapothula, Yu Xiang
